clue.text: Fellow is not dim

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
ain't is the colloquial contraction of is not

explanation.surface: Someone defends a chap's intelligence: he is not stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dim' reads as stupid in the surface, but here it means pale or weak, as a light is.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something barely visible or weakly lit, like a far-off glow.

clue.text: This castle has value in Texas

definitions.note: 'This ... in Texas' points to a place in that state, so the definition is a location

parts.note: a fort is a fortified stronghold, like a castle
worth means value

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on what a castle in Texas is worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This castle has value' builds the name, and 'in Texas' says it is a place there.
explanation.definitionFit: A large city in north Texas, neighbour of Dallas, bears this name.

clue.text: Lost hope because ra's ied pin exploded

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: ra's is read as the letters R, A, S

explanation.surface: Someone despaired because an improvised bomb went off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploded' shuffles RAS, IED and PIN; an IED is an improvised explosive device.
explanation.definitionFit: Having given up all expectation of things improving describes utter hopelessness.

clue.text: Caustic sailor wears particular shirt

parts.note: tar is an old word for a seaman
the T-shirt is a particular kind of shirt, giving T

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued seaman pulls on a T-shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wears' simply joins the sailor and the shirt letter; 'particular shirt' is a T-shirt, hence T.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, biting remark is acidic or sour in tone.

clue.text: Out in front of the wicket

definitions.text: Out in front of the wicket

parts.words: Out in front of the wicket
parts.note: a cricket dismissal where the batsman's leg stops a ball that would have hit the stumps, read as a description of position

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire's decision on a batsman standing at the stumps.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is out 'leg before wicket' (LBW) when the ball strikes the leg in line with the stumps; the clue reads both as a dismissal and a place.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the cricket mode of dismissal, short for leg before wicket, when a pad blocks a ball heading for the stumps.

clue.text: Is he a peer with a personal label

definitions.text: Is he a peer with a personal label

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm
privy means private or personal
a seal is a stamp or mark, like a label

explanation.surface: A question whether a nobleman has his own private emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The title is an ancient UK Cabinet office, once keeper of the monarch's personal seal.
explanation.definitionFit: This senior British government post was historically responsible for the sovereign's private stamp.

clue.text: Does he hesitate before being in charge?

indicators.note: before puts the hesitation sound ahead of the abbreviation

parts.note: er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A question about whether a man falters before taking command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he' is the definition: the answer is a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name stands for any man.

clue.text: Bulb in contact with charged particle

parts.note: on means touching, in contact with
an ion is an atom or molecule carrying electric charge

explanation.surface: A light bulb touching a charged particle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' suggests a light, but it is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A layered vegetable grows underground as a rounded storage organ.

clue.text: Eastern male encountered tourist in Cornwall

parts.note: met means encountered

explanation.surface: A man from the east bumps into a holidaymaker in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is a holiday county in the far south-west of England; locals there call visitors by this dialect word, which also means an ant.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cornish dialect the word for an ant is applied to the summer visitors who swarm in.

clue.text: Supplementary words of mountie, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a clause added to a document or bill as an amendment
a Canadian mounted policeman is one example of someone on horseback

explanation.definitionFit: An extra clause tacked onto a contract shares its name with anyone sitting on a horse, such as a Canadian mounted police officer.

clue.text: Mr sabbini rewrites Jewish doctrine

indicators.note: to rewrite something is to recast it, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A man named Mr Sabbini produces a new version of Jewish teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewrites' shuffles MR SABBINI; the name is invented purely as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The teachings and traditions of rabbis make up a body of Jewish religious thought.

clue.text: Unionists!

parts.note: not political supporters of union but the two people joined in a wedding

explanation.surface: A rallying cry for political supporters of union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unionists' suggests politics, especially in Northern Ireland; the exclamation mark says read it as a couple being united in marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The couple at a wedding are the two people being joined in matrimony.

clue.text: Cleanse starting with a soapy hand towel

definitions.text: Cleanse starting with a soapy hand towel

indicators.note: starting means the opening letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Instructions for cleaning yourself, beginning with a lathered flannel.
explanation.walkthrough: The heads of 'with a soapy hand' are W, A, S, H; the whole clue also pictures the act itself, with 'towel' finishing the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean with water and soap is the plain sense of this everyday verb.

clue.text: March past

parts.note: read not as a military parade but as the month that comes once March has gone by

explanation.surface: A ceremonial parade of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'march past' is a parade where troops file past a dignitary; read literally, it is the time after March.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth month of the year follows straight after the third.

clue.text: Ringing sound — switch over to buzzer

indicators.note: switching something over flips it end to end, so the word for the sound is read backwards

parts.note: a tang is a sharp ringing or twanging sound

explanation.surface: A ringing noise prompts someone to swap to an electric buzzer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch over' turns TANG back to front; 'buzzer' is not a doorbell but a small flying insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A small two-winged insect that whines and hums in flight is fairly called a buzzer.

clue.text: Travel smoothly like a short skier

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Travel smoothly like a short skier (5)': 'short' has no job and 'skier' gives no letters of the answer; probably the setter meant glider, but no source confirms the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Travel smoothly like a short skier

clue.text: Learn about king George's material

indicators.note: about means going round, so the verb for learning surrounds the other letters

parts.note: to see is to learn or find out
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king
George was the word for G in the old RAF phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone finds out about the cloth worn by King George.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps SEE round R and G; 'king George' looks like one person but gives two separate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A durable twilled woollen cloth is a fabric used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: Register of best achievement to date?

definitions.text: Register of best achievement to date?

parts.words: Register of best achievement to date?
parts.note: a whimsical gloss on a sporting or chart benchmark that has never been beaten, as if it were a written logbook

explanation.surface: A ledger listing the finest accomplishments so far.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'Register' is a playful take on the second word of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the best performance ever achieved, never yet surpassed, as in sport or music sales.

clue.text: Not straight! Not in! Out! Ref was confused

parts.note: out means not in, as of a batsman or a light

indicators.note: being confused means being mixed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A protest at a muddled referee who shouts out one moment and in the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was confused' shuffles OUT and REF; 'Not in' gives OUT as a separate first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bent or misaligned, off from the vertical or a straight line, is crooked.

clue.text: Does lover cook this fish?

indicators.note: to cook the books is to falsify, so cook signals the letters being doctored into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a lover would prepare this fish for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' looks like a kitchen verb but shuffles DOES LOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A prized flatfish caught in the English Channel is a classic seafood dish.

clue.text: Fab 4's demanding and conflicting work-pattern

parts.note: the Beatles' film and song title, read as a gruelling shift that is both day and night at once

explanation.surface: A gripe about the Beatles' punishing schedule of clashing shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fab Four are the Beatles; 'demanding' suggests hard, and a shift that is both day and night is 'conflicting'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of the Beatles' 1964 film, album and song, describing an exhausting stint of work.

clue.text: Brush hair of company doctor

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A firm's medical officer tidies someone's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom locks with a toothed tool is to tidy and smooth them.

clue.text: Tropic gets no wheat from Italian location

indicators.note: gets no means the grain is removed from the name of the tropic

parts.note: the Tropic of Capricorn is a line of latitude in the southern hemisphere
corn is a general word for cereal grain such as wheat

explanation.surface: A line of latitude yields no wheat for an Italian place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets no' takes CORN out of CAPRICORN, leaving an island off Naples.
explanation.definitionFit: The island in the Bay of Naples is a well-known place in Italy.

clue.text: She may sing many a song

definitions.text: She may sing many a song

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, hence many
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A singer may perform plenty of songs.
explanation.walkthrough: The heroine of 'West Side Story' and of 'The Sound of Music' sing many songs, and the name appears in songs too.
explanation.definitionFit: A female name borne by singing heroines in musicals stands for a woman who sings.

clue.text: Church official trimmed grass boundary

indicators.note: trimmed means cut short, so the final letter of the official's title is lopped off

parts.note: a verger is a caretaker and attendant in a church

explanation.surface: A church caretaker gives the edge of the lawn a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimmed' suits the grass in the surface but here docks the last letter of VERGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of turf along a road or path marks its edge.

clue.text: Fliers come back after a great distance

indicators.note: after places the returning airmen behind the letter A
coming back is returning, so the airmen's abbreviation is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, are airmen

explanation.surface: Airmen return from a long way off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come back' and 'after' are the two indicators; 'a great distance' stands for the adverb meaning 'at a great distance', as in 'from afar'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a long way off, describing remoteness rather than closeness.

clue.text: Tender voice of a Mercian ruler

indicators.note: voice of says the word is spoken, so its sound gives the spelling of the name

parts.note: to tender is to offer, as in tendering a bid

explanation.surface: The gentle speech of an Anglo-Saxon king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' reads as gentle but is the verb meaning to put forward; Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in central England whose king built a famous dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth-century king of Mercia ruled one of the great Anglo-Saxon kingdoms.

clue.text: Deeds of the apostles

parts.note: the doings of the early Christian disciples, which form the title of a New Testament book

explanation.surface: The works done by Jesus's followers.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifth book of the New Testament records what the apostles did after the Resurrection.
explanation.definitionFit: Things done are deeds, and the New Testament book on the apostles' work bears this title.

clue.text: Office case

definitions.meaning: a minister's area of responsibility in government
a flat carrying holder for papers or drawings

explanation.definitionFit: A government minister's area of responsibility shares its name with a flat case for carrying documents.

clue.text: Most inquisitive concerning item of bric-a-brac

indicators.note: most of a word means nearly all of it, so the last two letters of the synonym are dropped

parts.note: curious means eager to know, inquisitive

explanation.surface: The nosiest person asks about a knick-knack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most inquisitive' poses as a superlative, but 'Most' means only part of CURIOUS is used; 'concerning' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare or unusual small ornament prized as a collectable is a classic antique-shop find.

clue.text: Where dust may be isolated

definitions.meaning: inside a household cleaner that sucks up dirt
cut off from outside influence or context

explanation.definitionFit: Dirt ends up inside a suction cleaner, and the same phrase means cut off from everything around it.

clue.text: Obscene part of the play

indicators.note: part of means only a section of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A lewd episode in a stage drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit at the end of 'Obscene', and the whole clue also describes the answer as a section of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A division of an act in a stage drama is a unit of the play.
